title: Ash Dykes on his Congo Basin mission
description:
Ash Dykes has five Guinness World Records. He’s trekked through some of the world’s toughest environments. And he just can’t stop. The extreme adventurer has recently completed a 700km (434 mile) journey through the Congo Basin in central Africa by inflatable kayak. It was the first of six expeditions he’s doing back-to-back. The journey was documented ‘live’ on his socials.

So how do you prepare for challenges like this? Why do they seem to get tougher and tougher? Where is the limit? Ash joins us in the What in the World studio to talk about his mission, why he keeps raising the bar, and what he says to those who criticise him.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討極限探險家 Ash Dykes 完成 800 公里剛果盆地皮艇之旅的經驗。這項在社群媒體直播的旅程是其 Project 6 一年六項極限挑戰的第一站。訪談中， Ash Dykes 分享了他如何仰賴當地 Baka 部落與導遊的生存知識避開野生動物風險，並回應網友針對冒險真實性與通訊短暫中斷的質疑。最後，他也介紹了下一站將在零下 30 度低溫下騎馬橫越吉爾吉斯的籌備計畫。
summaryEn: In this episode of What in the World, extreme adventurer Ash Dykes discusses his recent 800 km inflatable kayak expedition through the Congo Basin, which he live-streamed as the first of six challenges in his 'Project 6' initiative. He explains how relying on the traditional survival knowledge of local guides and the Baka tribe helped his team safely navigate risks like hippos, elephants, and disease-carrying insects. Dykes also addresses online criticism regarding safety, claims of overhyping the danger, and a temporary satellite communications blackout during the trip, before sharing details about his upcoming winter expedition riding horses across Kyrgyzstan in minus 30-degree weather.
